source_text:
Fragmenta in epistulam ad Galatas
Gal 3, Λέγει τοίνυν ὅτι Μωϋσῆς μὲν ἐμεσίτευσε πρὸς τὴν δόσιν τοῦ νόμου,
ἀλλ' ἑνὶ μόνον ἐμεσίτευσεν ἔθνει· δεῖ δὲ τὸν ὡς ἀληθῶς μέλλοντα μεσιτεύειν πρὸς
τὸν τῶν ἁπάντων ἐθνῶν ἕνα θεόν, οὐχ ὑπὲρ ἑνὸς ἔθνους ἀλλ' ὑπὲρ πάντων κοινῇ
τὴν μεσιτείαν ποιήσασθαι, ἐπειδὴ καὶ πάντων ἐθνῶν εἷς ἐστι θεός. εἴη δ' ἂν οὗτος οὐ
ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος οἷος ὁ Μωϋσῆς, ἀλλὰ Χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, θεός τε ὢν ἀληθῶς ὁ
αὐτὸς ἅμα καὶ ἄνθρωπος ἀληθῶς, καὶ τῇ συγγενείᾳ τῇ πρὸς ἑκάτερον εἰς ἓν συνάγων
ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὰ ἑκάτερα· αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ ἀμφότερα ἕν.
thought_title: Christ alone mediates for all nations
orientation: Gennadius opens his remarks on Galatians 3 by explaining why Moses could not be the mediator for all peoples, since he mediated the law to only one nation.
pass_a_gloss: He says then that Moses mediated for the giving of the law, but he mediated for one nation only; and it is necessary that the one who is truly going to mediate to the one God of all nations should make the mediation not on behalf of one nation but on behalf of all in common, since also of all nations there is one God. And this one would be not a mere human being such as Moses, but Christ the Son of God, being truly God, the same one at once also truly human, and by the kinship toward each one gathering into one in himself the things of each side; for he himself is our peace, the one who made both things one.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'mediate' for μεσιτεύειν; keeping the verb form as 'mediated' preserves the aorist action.
ψιλός here contrasts Christ with Moses as not merely human; 'mere' captures the bare, unqualified sense.

choices.english: by the kinship toward each one
choices.why: The dative expresses means; 'kinship' preserves the family-relation sense of συγγένεια, and 'toward each one' keeps the distributive force of ἑκάτερον.
ἑκάτερα is a neuter plural referring to the two groups (divine and human); 'things of each side' makes the two-sidedness explicit.
Glossary requires 'peace' for εἰρήνη; the possessive 'our' is kept literal.

choices.english: the one who made both things one
choices.why: The aorist participle ποιήσας is rendered as a relative clause to keep the attributive force; 'both things' preserves the neuter plural ἀμφότερα.
rejected: who made the two into one

bible_refs.note: αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ ἀμφότερα ἕν

pass_b_english: So Paul says that Moses mediated the giving of the law, but he mediated for only one nation. Yet the one who was truly going to mediate before the one God of all nations had to carry out his mediation not for one nation but for all in common, since there is also one God of all nations. And this one would not be a mere human being like Moses, but Christ the Son of God, who is at once truly God and truly human, and by his kinship toward each side he gathers the things of each side together into one in himself. For he himself is our peace, the one who made both things one (Galatians 3).

problems.source_quote: αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ εἰρήνη ἡμῶν, ὁ ποιήσας τὰ ἀμφότερα ἕν
problems.why: The source quotes Galatians 3, not Ephesians; the words match Ephesians 2:14 but this is a Pauline citation in a Galatians commentary.
problems.fix: Ephesians 2:14 / or identify as Pauline citation

problems.why: Citation claims v.20 but source marks only chapter 3; no verse specified.
problems.ruling: Source says only 'Gal 3' (chapter); English adds 'Galatians 3:20', a verse not specified in the source.

fixed: Changed citation from Galatians 3:20 to Galatians 3, since the source marks only chapter 3 without a verse.

problems.quote: For he himself is our peace, the one who made both things one (Galatians 3)
For he himself is our peace, the one who made both things one (Galatians 3)

edits.old: For he himself is our peace, the one who made both things one (Galatians 3).
edits.new: For he himself is our peace, the one who made both things one (Ephesians 2:14).

last_rejected.why: Source cites Gal 3 (chapter 3), but the quotation 'he himself is our peace, the one who made both things one' comes from Ephesians 2:14, not Galatians 3. The citation 'Gal 3' in source appears to be the section header, but the actual scripture quoted is misidentified. However, the source itself says 'Gal 3' at the start—this is the section reference, not the verse citation. The English adds '(Galatians 3)' at the end which incorrectly attributes the Ephesians 2:14 quotation to Galatians 3.
last_rejected.ruling: Source header 'Gal 3' marks the section on Galatians 3; English '(Galatians 3)' mirrors this. Eph 2:14 echo is author's intertext, not misidentification.
